# A spacer grows into the room its siblings leave, as `flex: 1` does, and a
# `flex` of its own is its share.
#
# On bubbletea a spacer grew only where its Style named a flex, so a toolbar's
# bare spacer pushed nothing and the label after it sat beside the one before.
# The snapshot is the screen as text.

env SNGL_UPDATE_SNAPSHOTS=1
sngl test --platform=bubbletea app.sngl
stdout 'PASS'
! stdout 'FAIL'
# a bare spacer takes the whole of a 30-column row's free space.
grep '(?m)^a {28}b$' app.sngl.snapshots/row.ansi
# beside a spacer of flex 2, one of flex 1 takes a third: 27 free, 9 and 18.
grep '(?m)^c {9}d {18}e$' app.sngl.snapshots/row.ansi

-- app.sngl --
import test "sngl:test"
import ui "sngl:ui"

output { go { bubbletea } }

component row ui.node {
    ui.vbox {
        ui.hbox(style={width=240px}) {
            ui.text(value="a")
            ui.spacer
            ui.text(value="b")
        }
        ui.hbox(style={width=240px}) {
            ui.text(value="c")
            ui.spacer
            ui.text(value="d")
            ui.spacer(style={flex=2})
            ui.text(value="e")
        }
    }
}

func testRow(t test.Test, c row) {
    t.snapshot("row")
}

ui.window {
    row
}
-- testrun/bubbletea/go/app.sngl/row/1 --
